currentUse: No living Wilkes-Barre All Saints Lithuanian national Catholic congregation has been established in current denominational rosters. A church building and memorial stone are documented historically, but the exact address, current owner, present use, and physical condition remain unresolved.
summary: Wilkes-Barre's Visų Šventųjų (All Saints) was a distinct Lithuanian national or independent Catholic parish, separate from the city's Roman Catholic Holy Trinity parish. A 1984 Draugas history lists a durable Wilkes-Barre national parish and gives 1929, while later field documentation associates the church with a 1932 cornerstone. Those dates may describe different stages—organization and building—but the surviving evidence does not yet resolve them. A 2022 Draugas heritage article documented a memorial stone on the wall of the Lithuanian national church, proving that the physical site remained identifiable at that time. Current Polish National Catholic Church directories do not list a Wilkes-Barre All Saints congregation, and a Lithuanian National Catholic history identifies Scranton's Providence of God as the surviving Lithuanian national parish. No closure act, legal successor, deed, exact address, current ownership, demolition record, or present building use has been established, so the profile records a historical parish and an unresolved physical outcome rather than claiming that the church is gone.

historicalNarrative.text: All Saints belonged to the Lithuanian national Catholic movement that created parishes outside Roman Catholic diocesan control. In Wilkes-Barre it formed a separate institution from Holy Trinity, the city's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish. Later retrospective evidence lists the Wilkes-Barre national parish among the movement's durable congregations and assigns it the year 1929.

historicalNarrative.text: A second date enters through the physical record. Heritage fieldwork identifies an All Saints Lithuanian National Catholic church and reports a 1932 cornerstone. The difference from the 1929 retrospective may reflect an organizing date followed by construction, but that explanation remains an inference until a charter, building permit, deed, or contemporary dedication account is found.

historicalNarrative.text: The parish left a visible material trace. A 2022 Draugas heritage article identified a commemorative stone on the wall of the Wilkes-Barre Lithuanian national church. That evidence supports the existence and continued identifiability of a building at the time of the visit, but it does not establish legal ownership, current religious use, or whether the structure remains in the same condition today.

historicalNarrative.text: The living institutional line has ended or become untraceable. The current Central Diocese directory of the Polish National Catholic Church contains no Wilkes-Barre All Saints parish, while a Lithuanian National Catholic history identifies Scranton's Providence of God parish—not Wilkes-Barre—as the surviving Lithuanian congregation. These sources support an inactive historical status, but directory absence cannot supply an exact closure date or prove a merger into Scranton.

historicalNarrative.text: The parish's terminal history remains an open research problem. No closure decree, incorporation record, deed, exact street address, successor instrument, cemetery record, or current property source has been located. The profile therefore keeps the church's physical outcome as unknown and does not turn later Scranton continuity into a legal succession claim for Wilkes-Barre.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The All Saints identity and Lithuanian national Catholic class are supported. The source dates conflict or describe different stages: Draugas gives 1929 for the parish, while field evidence reports a 1932 cornerstone. Neither date should silently displace the other. A 2022 report supports a still-identifiable church and memorial stone, but no official current property source has established the building's present condition. Scranton's surviving national parish is a sister institution, not a documented legal successor.
gaps: No charter, incorporation record, deed, exact street address, clergy roster, parish register, closure act, legal successor instrument, current ownership record, present-use documentation, or demolition evidence has been found. Luzerne County property and city-directory research is needed before assigning a terminal building condition.
